# Songwriting & AI Music Generation

Everything here is a GUIDELINE, not a rule. Art breaks rules on purpose.
Use what serves the song. Ignore what doesn't.

## 1. Song Structure

Common skeletons: ABABCB (Verse/Chorus/Verse/Chorus/Bridge/Chorus), AABA,
ABAB, and AAA. Structure serves the emotion rather than acting as a fixed rule.

The six building blocks are Intro, Verse, Pre-Chorus, Chorus, Bridge and Outro.
You don't need all of them; sections can evolve or be omitted when that serves the song.

## 2. Rhyme, Meter, and Sound

Use perfect, family, assonant, consonant and near/slant rhymes in combination.
Internal rhyme can create additional musical connection. Matching stressed syllables
between parallel lines usually matters more than exact syllable counts.

Read or sing lines aloud. If the mouth naturally stumbles, revise the meter. Intentional
meter breaks are allowed when they create emphasis.

## 3. Emotional Arc and Dynamics

Think of a song as a journey. Contrast creates impact: sparse before dense, quiet before
loud, slow before fast, and silence before a payoff. A whisper-to-roar-to-whisper arc can
work for intimate songs and anthems alike.

## 4. Lyrics and Hooks

Prefer concrete imagery when it serves the emotion. The hook is the memorable phrase,
usually connected to the title or core idea. Place it where the melody and emotion make
it land hardest.

Prosody matters: stable feelings can use settled melodies and resolved language; unstable
feelings can use wandering melodies or unresolved phrasing. Revision is part of creation.

## 5. Adaptation and Parody

When adapting an existing work, map structure, syllables, rhyme and stressed beats first.
Do not copy protected lyrics. Create new wording and use structural analysis only to guide
original writing.

## 6. Suno AI Prompt Engineering

A useful style formula is:
Genre + Mood + Era + Instruments + Vocal Style + Production + Dynamics.

Describe the musical journey rather than listing genres only. Specify BPM and key when
needed. Describe vocal persona and production dynamics. Avoid artist names and trademarks;
describe musical characteristics instead.

Useful lyric metatags include:
[Intro] [Verse] [Pre-Chorus] [Chorus] [Bridge] [Outro]
[Whispered] [Spoken Word] [Belted] [Falsetto] [Breathy] [Harmonies]
[High Energy] [Low Energy] [Building Energy] [Explosive] [Emotional Climax]
[Female Vocals] [Male Vocals]

Use a small, coherent set of tags and do not contradict them in the same section.

## 7. Phonetic Tricks

AI singers respond to written pronunciation. Spell unusual words phonetically when
necessary, guide syllable boundaries with hyphens, and test proper nouns early.

Spell numbers out when pronunciation matters. Fix pronunciation in the lyrics before
generation because the generated performance bakes in many pronunciation decisions.

## 8. Workflow

1. Define the concept and hook.
2. If adapting, map structure without copying lyrics.
3. Brainstorm raw material.
4. Draft lyrics into a structure.
5. Read or sing the draft aloud.
6. Build the Suno style description.
7. Add restrained metatags.
8. Generate multiple variations.
9. Keep the strongest take and revise weak sections.
10. Restate important genre/mood constraints when extending a track.
